title: SAE Feature Splitting Rates Across Layers: Are Early Layers More or Less Polysemantic Than Late Layers?

original_idea.problem: A systematic layer-by-layer SAE comparison is missing from published literature for small open-source models.
original_idea.direction: Train matched SAEs on every other layer of GPT-2-small using SAELens. Measure L0 sparsity, dead feature fraction, feature splitting counts, and downstream loss recovery. Plot versus layer depth.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Plausible chain: if polysemanticity concentrates in specific layers, interpretability efforts can be targeted, reducing compute for full-model interpretability. The safety connection is through improved interpretability tool efficiency rather than direct risk reduction.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: SAELens provides a framework for SAE training on GPT-2-small. Existing checkpoints provide baselines. However, training 6 SAEs with matched hyperparameters and computing feature splitting metrics requires familiarity with SAE methodology. Intermediate level with good tooling support.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Six SAE training runs (can be parallelized on medium compute), four metrics per layer, one plot. Clear deliverable: layer-depth vs. polysemanticity chart. Well-bounded. Each SAE training on GPT-2-small is ~1-2 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Open-source SAEs for all residual stream layers in GPT-2 Small exist (Alignment Forum), and basic layer-dependent statistics (L0 sparsity ranging from 5 to 70, dead feature counts) have been reported. OpenAI's 'Scaling and Evaluating Sparse Autoencoders' provides evaluation methodology. However, a systematic layer-by-layer comparison of feature splitting counts specifically — how many polysemantic features split into monosemantic ones as dictionary size increases — has not been published as a focused study. The L0 and dead feature trends are known; the splitting rate metric adds incremental novelty.
